title.narrative: Danish support for the work of the UN Secretary General's Climate Action Team on combatting climate change

description.narrative:
The objective of this development cooperation between the Government of Denmark and the Secretary General’s Climate Action Team is to support the teams activities targeted at ODA-eligible countries. The objectives of the development cooperation include:
1. Country Engagement to advance progress on delivery of ambitious NDCs and Net Zero Strategies, with a focus on climate vulnerable countries.
2. Continued Push on Energy Transitions-- No New Coal.
3. Maintain pressure on public finance commitments of ODA and the US$100B commitment.

title.narrative: Output indicator 2 Scaled up adaptation and resilience finance and projects in developing countries including through cooperative initiatives such as the adaptation pipeline accelerator (APA), with CAT providing political guidance and oversight The SG's Early Warning Systems for all (EWS4ALL) initiative has expanded work on early warning systems in 30 underserved countries, with CAT political guidance and oversight, and in collaboration with other partners and initiatives.

target.value: -Only half of countries globally are protected by multi-hazard early warning systems. Only a third of Small Island Developing States, and less than half of the Least Developed Countries and Africa have such systems. -No countries covered by Adaptation Pipeline Accelerator (APA) initiative

-In 30 focus countries, the EWS4ALL initiative has been initiated starting to connect existing initiatives in the field with clear country-action plans and funding mechanism to finance the action plans. -APA initiative launched in 4 developing countries.
-Demonstrated progress of EW4ALL in 30 countries of first cohort with tangible improvements in EWS capabilities. -APA initiative expanded to 10 developing countries.

-APA initiative expanded to 15 developing countries. -In additional 30 countries (cohort 3), the EWS4ALL initiative has been rolled-out connecting all existing initiatives in the field with clear country-action plans and funding mechanism to finance the action plans. Implementation progressing in 60 first and second cohort countries with tangible improvements in EWS capabilities.
-APA initiative expanded to 20 developing countries. -Globally all countries are covered by multi-hazard early warinng systems.

title.narrative: A strategy on implementing United Nations' Secretary-General's Climate Action Priorities supporting the full realization of the long-term goals of the Paris Agreement is developed and executed.

Availability of the strategy and evidence of its successful execution, including: - Global GHG emissions peak in 2025 and decline thereafter to be halved by 2030 - ODA eligible countries have an increased ability to adapt to the adverse impacts of climate change and foster climate resilience and low greenhouse gas emissions development, in a manner that does not threaten food production. This is measured by levels of funding and capacity building for adaptation projects in ODA eligible countries - Finance flows consistent with a pathway towards net zero greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development.

target.value: -Global GHG emissions have peaked by 2025 and start declining -Adaptation needs are 90% covered in ODA -eligible countries, especially through access to early warning systems-Global financial flows are more aligned with 1.5C consistent net-zero pathways and covers needs for net zero transition especially in ODA-eligible developing countries
